private_note: Birch (52) and Hazel (50) still pay me more than Alder (48), but the poll settles it: seven upper and middle votes for Cedar, and 1, 5 and 10 all name Alder as their fallback. Add the five of us below the middle and Alder is at eight. Birch has no path to nine. Alder beats Today by 2 and guarantees health coverage. Cedar is worse than failure. I'm moving to Alder now to show the bloc and win over 12, 6, 3 or 9.
statement: Round 1 told us something. Cedar has seven votes, and it can't get past seven: five of us lose under it and won't vote for it. Birch and Hazel can't get nine either. Delegates 1, 5 and 10 said Alder is where they'd meet us. Delegates 2, 4, 7 and 8 said they'd back it over walking away. So I'm moving my first choice to Alder this round, and I'd ask everyone below the middle to do the same so the poll shows it. That makes eight. We need one more. Delegates 3, 6, 9 and 12: Alder leaves the economy running as it does now and costs the top groups only a little. Failure leaves today's system in place for a generation, with no guaranteed floor and millions uninsured. If nine of us want a deal, Alder is the one plan that can get there. Tell us what it would take.
